title: Finite separable specialization of an open family of norm pencils
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-curve of dimension one, $G$ a finite group acting by $F$-automorphisms, $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module, and $n\geq1$. Put $B=\bigotimes_{g\in G}g^*L$ and use the norm sections $\mathcal N_G$ of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]. Assume $V=\Gamma(C,L^{\otimes n})$ is finite dimensional. Let $W\subseteq V\times V$ be a nonempty Zariski open, where $V\times V$ denotes affine space after a choice of basis. Suppose that for every extension field $T/F$ and $(a,b)\in W(T)$ the norm pair generates $B_T^{\otimes n}$ and defines a finite surjective $G$-invariant morphism $\psi_{a,b}:C_T\to\mathbf P^1_T$ etale on a nonempty open. Let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed subscheme. Then there exist a finite separable extension $E/F$, a pair $(a,b)\in W(E)$, and $g\in\mathrm{SL}_2(E)$ such that $g\circ\psi_{a,b}:C_E\to\mathbf P^1_E$ is finite, surjective, $G$-invariant and etale on a nonempty open, and its fibres above $[0:1],[1:1],[1:0]$ are finite etale over $E$, with reduced union disjoint from $M_E$. This holds even when $F$ is finite. The group fixes the extended constants $E$. A finite separable extension is a finite-dimensional extension all of whose elements have separable minimal polynomial; $\mathrm{SL}_2(E)$ is the group of determinant-one two-by-two matrices over $E$.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-base-change], [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-pc-module-pullback], [def-kun-projective], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change].

source.place: de Jong §3.4, printed p.606; agent-written quotient-free norm-section replacement, extracted from returned proof steps 15--16. proof.text: Choose a basis of $V$, so $V\times V=\mathbf A^{2d}_F$ for $d=\dim_F V$. This affine space is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and its open subscheme $W$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a). Since $W$ is nonempty, [lem-pc-dense-separable-points] gives a closed point $w\in W$ with $F_1=\kappa(w)$ finite separable over $F$. Its residue-field morphism is the desired pair $(a,b)\in W(F_1)$. The hypothesis of the item now gives the finite surjective invariant pencil $\psi_1:C_{F_1}\to\mathbf P^1_{F_1}$, etale on a nonempty open.

By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois] choose a separable closure $K/F_1$, which is Galois and separably closed. By [lem-sfb-separably-closed-field-infinite], $K$ is infinite. Applying [lem-pd-geometric-curve] to the original curve and the separable closure $K/F$ gives that $C_K$ is again a smooth projective geometrically integral curve of dimension one: $K/F$ is separable algebraic by [lem-zl-separable-permanence], and is separably closed. Thus it is a separable closure of $F$ as well. The genus in that lemma is simply the genus of $C$; no specified genus is required here.

source.place: Tags 09GT, 09HC, 09HB; geometric-curve base change as in lem-pd-geometric-curve

proof.text: The base change $M_K\subset C_K$ is closed by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change], finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). It is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced], since $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is reduced. The image of $(a,b)$ is in $W(K)$ by composition of its point morphism with $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F_1$. Thus the hypothesis also gives a finite surjective invariant pencil $\psi_K:C_K\to\mathbf P^1_K$, etale on a nonempty open.

For every intermediate extension $T/F_1$, the pencil of the image of $(a,b)$ in $W(T)$ is $(\psi_1)_T$. In [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm], retain the same finite enumeration of $G$. On an open where the finitely many translated line bundles are trivial, a translated section has a coefficient $u_g$, and its tensor has coefficient $\prod_g u_g$. Scalar extension sends this to $\prod_g(u_g\otimes1)$: this follows recursively from $u\mapsto1\otimes u$ and the tensor multiplication rule. The recursively defined pullback-power and tensor-distribution comparisons only regroup these factors, so the norm sections themselves pull back to the norm sections over $T$. Write their local coefficients as $A,B$. On the projective charts the morphism of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is given by $A/B$ where $B$ is invertible and $B/A$ where $A$ is invertible. Scalar extension gives $(A\otimes1)/(B\otimes1)$ and its inverse on those same pulled-back charts. Since the pair generates, these charts cover the source; hence the morphisms agree. This computes only the pulled-back chosen sections, without asserting base change for the entire space of global sections. In particular $\psi_K=(\psi_1)_K$.

source.place: Agent norm-section replacement of §3.4, base-change compatibility from the definitions

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-integral-coordinate-avoidance] with $A=K$, fraction field $K$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $Y=C_K$, pencil $\psi_K$, and marking $M_K$. All its hypotheses were verified in steps 2--3. It gives $h\in\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ such that $h\circ\psi_K$ has finite etale fibres at $0,1,\infty$, with reduced union disjoint from $M_K$. Invariance is retained. This use is only of the infinite-domain avoidance lemma; no family or finite-separable specialization assertion is assumed.

source.place: §3.4, printed p.606, coordinate avoidance, applied over the separable closure

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] to the four matrix entries of $h$ in the Galois extension $K/F_1$. Obtain $F_1\subseteq E\subseteq K$ finite Galois over $F_1$ containing these entries. Their matrix $g$ over $E$ has determinant one, since its determinant maps to $\det h=1$ under the injective field map $E\hookrightarrow K$. The original pair gives $(a,b)\in W(E)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] and [lem-zl-separable-permanence], the tower $F\subseteq F_1\subseteq E$ is finite separable over $F$.

Put $\varphi_E=g\circ\psi_{a,b}$. The matrix inverse $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}g_{22}&-g_{12}\\-g_{21}&g_{11}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ defines the inverse projective automorphism. Thus composing with $g$ preserves finiteness and surjectivity: on affine charts the coordinate ring map of this isomorphism is an isomorphism, so a finite module remains finite; surjectivity follows from bijectivity. It preserves $G$-invariance because $\psi_{a,b}\circ\sigma=\psi_{a,b}$ implies $g\circ\psi_{a,b}\circ\sigma=g\circ\psi_{a,b}$. The isomorphism $g$ identifies its source with the whole (open) target, hence is an open immersion and is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). Clause (2) of that same node shows that $\varphi_E$ is etale on the nonempty open supplied for $\psi_{a,b}$ by the hypothesis.

source.place: §3.4, elementary composition with a projective coordinate automorphism

proof.text: For $t\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ let $D_t=\varphi_E^{-1}(t)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre. It is finite over $E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). By step 4 and $g_K=h$, its base change to $K$ is the corresponding finite etale fibre of step 5. The map $(D_t)_K\to D_t$ is surjective: it is the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}E$, which is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective], using [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. For every $x\in D_t$ choose a point $x_K$ above it and apply [lem-sc-etale-faithfully-flat-local] to $D_t\to\operatorname{Spec}E$. It follows that this map is etale at every point, hence etale. This checks descent on the fibre schemes themselves; it does not infer etaleness from reducedness alone.

source.place: Tags 01WL, 01S1; pointwise field-extension descent as in lem-sc-etale-faithfully-flat-local

proof.text: Each $D_t$ is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. The three distinct rational target points have disjoint fibres, so their scheme-theoretic union is their finite disjoint union, and is reduced. If this union met $M_E$, the intersection would acquire a point after base change to $K$, by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Its base change is the empty intersection from step 5, a contradiction. Hence the union is disjoint from $M_E$. The action on every scalar extension is $\sigma\times\mathrm{id}$, so it fixes $E$ pointwise. The argument used finite-separable residue points and a separable closure, never the existence of an $F$-rational parameter or infinitely many elements of $F$; it therefore includes finite $F$, the empty marking, and trivial or nonfaithful $G$.
